zh.title: 美國航空兩客機使用同呼號重疊飛行 FAA展開調查
zh.summary: 美國航空兩架737客機於鳳凰城使用相同呼號飛行；FAA對此展開調查
body: 美國航空（American Airlines）兩架波音737-800型客機，於2026年8月14日午夜剛過，在美國鳳凰城天港國際機場（PHX）附近的相同空域內，使用完全相同的空中交通管制呼號「American 2482」同時飛行。美國聯邦航空管理局（FAA）目前已對此一呼號重複事件展開調查。

根據航班資料與相關通報，其中一架客機當時正自芝加哥奧黑爾（ORD）國際機場飛抵鳳凰城並下降至11,000呎；另一架客機則剛從鳳凰城起飛準備前往芝加哥，正攀升至9,000呎。這起呼號重複事件起因於自芝加哥飛往鳳凰城的入境航班因天候因素延誤，原定晚間10時43分抵達，實際於凌晨12時13分才降落。美國航空為了避免延誤後續回程服務，調派另一架已在鳳凰城當地的波音737-800客機執行起飛任務。在預期可能發生呼號重複的情況下，標準程序通常會在推開前重新申報不同航班號碼或在呼號後方附加字母，但此次並未採取相關措施。
當該管制區域的空中交通管制員與機組員發現呼號重疊後，管制員隨即採用「American 2482進場機」與「American 2482離場機」的方式分別向兩架客機進行呼號辨識與空中指引。管制員將離場客機高度限制在9,000呎，同時保持進場客機在其上方高度飛行，並持續向雙方機組發送航情通告。兩機機組員隨後均回報目視發現對方空中目標。
美國聯邦航空管理局表示，兩架航機在整個過程中均維持了法定要求的安全間隔，且均未接獲空中防撞系統（TCAS）的決斷警報（RA）。美國航空發表聲明指出，公司目前正針對相關情況進行內部檢討，並對管制員與自身機組員在過程中成功維持航機安全間隔表示肯定。

en.title: FAA Probes Two American Airlines Boeing 737s Flying Under Same Callsign Near Phoenix
en.summary: American Airlines Boeing 737s flew under identical callsigns near Phoenix, prompting an FAA investigation.
body: Two American Airlines Boeing 737-800 aircraft were airborne under the identical callsign "American 2482" in the same sector near Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (PHX) shortly after midnight on August 14, 2026. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has initiated an investigation into the callsign duplication.

One aircraft was arriving from Chicago O'Hare International Airport (ORD) and descending through 11,000 feet, while the other had just departed Phoenix for Chicago O'Hare and was climbing toward 9,000 feet. The callsign duplication arose after weather delayed the inbound flight from Chicago, which landed at 12:13 a.m. local time compared to its scheduled arrival time of 10:43 p.m. Rather than holding the return flight, American Airlines dispatched a second Boeing 737-800 already on the ground at Phoenix. When a duplication is anticipated, standard procedure is to refile the second flight under a different number or append a letter to the callsign before pushback, but neither step was taken.

Once the conflict became apparent, the sector air traffic controller addressed the flights as "American 2482 on the arrival" and "American 2482 on the departure" to differentiate between the two aircraft. The controller restricted the departing jet to 9,000 feet while keeping the arriving aircraft at a higher altitude above it, passing traffic advisories to both flight crews until both reported having the other aircraft in sight.

The FAA confirmed that required separation was maintained between the two aircraft throughout the encounter, and neither aircraft received a collision avoidance resolution advisory. American Airlines stated that it is reviewing the circumstances surrounding the flight and credited both air traffic controllers and its own flight crews with maintaining required aircraft separation.
